newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom, FCL Building slide as NZ shares end lower.
newsitem.headline: Telecom, FCL Building slide as NZ shares end lower.

text.p: * NZ shares end lower on second day of high volume
* Fletcher results seen as "mixed bag", Building punished

New Zealand shares closed lower on high volume on Wednesday as Telecom continued its slide and the market reacted with disappointment to first-half earnings from the four Fletcher Challenge companies.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 10.34 points lower at 2,290.14.

Telecom soaked up further punishment on ongoing concerns about its earnings growth prospects after last week's disappointing third quarter result. The shares ended at $6.50, their lowest level since August 15.
In the Fletcher group, the focus was on the Building letter stock, which fell 14 cents to $4.13 after reporting a sharp fall in interim net profit to NZ$53 million from $77 million.

The other FCL stocks also lost ground on results that County Natwest's Sean Vaughan described as "a mixed bag of nuts". But he said Paper, down three at $2.90, had held up reasonably well after reporting a first-half loss of NZ$40 million when analysts had expected a result around break-even.

Energy shed a cent to $3.82. "The Energy result was probably ahead of expectations, but on the other hand the oil price has peaked and it's a commodity stock," said Cavill White's Richard Burton. He said that brokerage sees Paper and Forest as around fair value, and sees Building as worth around $4.10.

Burton said the high market turnover suggested some investors saw good buying at these levels. "Where people are comfortable that earnings are reasonably sustainable, they're in there buying, but it's not an easy market," he said.
Tranz Rail gained another 15 cents to $8.65, reflecting what Burton called a flight towards quality of earnings.
